Inclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Criterion: Concurrent Medication: Allowed: - Procrit. - Amphotericin B (1 mg/kg up to 5 days/week). - Prophylaxis treatment as per ACTG recommendations for Pneumocystis carinii pneumonia. - Acyclovir (up to 1000 mg/day PO; for > 1000 mg/day PO or for any IV dose, suggest interrupting ddC). - Ketoconazole (up to 10 mg/kg/day). - Nystatin. - Aspirin, acetaminophen, sedatives, and barbiturates (for up to 72 hours). - Isoniazid (INH), if there is no evidence of peripheral neuropathy at entry. Children should receive pyridoxine, 25 - 50 mg/day to avoid possible INH-associated neuropathy. - Trimethoprim / sulfamethoxazole (T/S). - Immunoglobulin therapy. - Aerosolized pentamidine. - Drugs with little nephro-, hepato-, cytotoxicity that the patient has been taking and tolerating well for an ongoing condition.
Inclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Justification: The patient is on metformin (diabetes) and statins (hypercholesterolemia), both of which are generally well-tolerated with low nephrotoxicity/hepatotoxicity. No excluded medications are present.

Inclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Criterion: Concurrent Treatment: Allowed: - Immunoglobulin therapy. - Nutritional support (for children with wasting syndrome and/or malnutritional) including hyperalimentation (TPN) of dietary supplements.
Inclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Justification: The patient is not explicitly stated to be on immunoglobulin therapy or nutritional support, but the criteria allow these as optional treatments. No data confirms or denies their use.

Inclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Criterion: Patients must have the following: - Absence of acute opportunistic infection at time of entry. - However, if patient is successfully treated for opportunistic infection and has remained stable for 2 weeks after treatment, the patient is then allowed to enter the study. Inclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Justification: The criteria allow these as optional treatments, but the patient is not on them. The criterion is about allowed treatments, not required ones.

Inclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Criterion: Prior Medication: AMENDED: - AZT or ddI up until study entry, other antiretrovirals up until 4 weeks of study entry Allowed: - Zidovudine (AZT) within 4 weeks of entry. - Dideoxyinosine (ddI) within 43 weeks of entry if no peripheral neuropathy has been observed while receiving ddI. - Other toxicities observed while on ddI must resolve to level 2 or better before patient can begin treatment with ddC. - Vitamin, folate, iron supplements.
Inclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Justification: The patient is not on AZT, ddI, or other antiretrovirals. No data contradicts this.

Exclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Justification: No mention of seizures or anticonvulsant therapy.

Exclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Justification: No evidence of acute bacterial infections.
No mention of hypersensitivity to ddC.

Exclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Justification: No evidence of active opportunistic infections requiring excluded medications.

Exclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Justification: No evidence of experimental therapies or drugs causing these effects.

Recap: The patient meets most inclusion criteria, including absence of acute opportunistic infections and written consent. However, the exclusion criterion for 'symptomatic cardiomyopathy' is unclear due to insufficient data on symptoms. No other exclusion criteria are violated.
